findings.trigger: Promote with ACCEPTANCE_RECORD whose record_ref points to any existing non-review document containing the claimed reviewer string and 'appoint'/'commission'; appointment_ref any real commit; subject_sha any real unrelated commit; scope node or '*'.
findings.observed: Code-inspected: caller-supplied reviewer/author/subject/assertion fields are trusted. record_ref only needs an existing blob containing the claimed principal or role plus 'appoint'/'commission'; appointment_ref only needs to be a commit; scope '*' bypasses node scope; node.subject_sha is optional. JOIN_E_7BF has no subject_sha (programma_p1_seed.py:172), so any real subject passes. The implementation return itself contains 'JOIN-V' and 'appointment' and can serve as the record.
findings.requirement: Acceptance must bind an independently established reviewer principal/role, distinct author, exact subject, assertion, scope and competent appointment/intake record; caller-written claims and unrelated genuine commits cannot supply it.
findings.smallest_fix: Parse acceptance from the referenced immutable record; require a registered independent review/appointment (for example the JOIN-V blob and appointment seal); require exact subject/scope and a node subject_sha; reject '*' and unregistered record_refs. Apply the gate at build or downgrade seed acceptance claims to reported/unverified.

findings.trigger: Modify seed_oscience_patch.json after GENESIS while keeping its declared count structure, then run rebuild or verify-journal.
findings.observed: Code-inspected: _apply_event passes the event's patch_digest to ingest_oscience; ingest_oscience uses 'patch_digest or _digest(patch)' but never recomputes and compares the actual file digest. A changed patch is imported under the old digest; verify-journal still passes because it checks only the journal chain.
findings.requirement: Cold replay must detect tampered inputs and reconstruct the same semantic state.
findings.smallest_fix: Always recompute _digest(patch); fail closed when it differs from payload.patch_digest, or embed the full patch in the event.

findings.trigger: Remove the last complete journal line, leaving a valid hash-chained prefix, then run a normal read or verify-journal.
findings.observed: Code-inspected: read_journal accepts any valid prefix; _load_state sees disk journal_head/revision differ from the shorter journal and silently rebuilds and saves the shorter state. Accepted events are lost without an error. The existing test only removes the final newline.
findings.requirement: Cold replay must detect truncated inputs and not lose accepted events.
findings.smallest_fix: Persist a monotonic expected journal head/revision separately and fail closed on regression, or require explicit recover intent; add a test dropping a complete final event.

findings.trigger: Mark P1_B_MATERIAL_SOURCE review FAILED, withdraw and restore that source, then inspect P1_LATER_HELP_CONSUMER.

findings.trigger: Two concurrent commit_event writers rebuild and save the derived state.
findings.observed: Code-inspected: commit_event saves without expected_revision; _save's optional CAS is a non-atomic read-check-write. A stale writer can overwrite a newer derived state. probe_faults exercises concurrent journal appends only, not concurrent state saves.
findings.requirement: Use revision/CAS and recoverable writes so stale concurrent updates do not lose accepted state.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass expected_revision through commit_event and retry on StaleStateRevision, or serialize the state CAS with the journal lock; add a concurrent state-write probe.
